# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +859
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +859
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +859
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

Now I have a good picture of the changes. Let me now do the deep-dive review. Key areas to check:

1. **The image cap resolution in `_buildRequestContext`**: it uses `imageCapOverride ?? resolveImageCap(modelId: config.model.id, catalogMaxImages: config.model.maxImages)`. Note that `resolveImageCap` reads the process-wide `imageRegistryConfig.perModel` — but NOT the `imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest` issue. Wait, actually it does fall back to `imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest`. That's fine.

  BUT: one subtle issue — the doc in agent_loop.dart says "latched > perModel config > catalog maxImages > the global maxPerRequest". The `overrideFor` returns the latch or null; then `resolveImageCap` reads perModel from process-wide `imageRegistryConfig` — this ignores the `ImageRegistryConfig` that was potentially loaded per-host... it IS the process-wide config. OK.

2. **Ordering issue in `healIfNeeded`**: `_needsImageCapHeal` requires `classifyImageCapError(finished.errorMessage) != null`. Then `healIfNeeded` sets `healed = true` BEFORE checking `refusal.learnedCap < 1`. If the cap is degenerate (<1), it returns false — one-shot spent? Actually the docstring says "A degenerate learned cap (< 1, garbage is 0) is refusal-family only: no re-send, the error surfaces as today (E3)." Setting healed=true and returning false means... it's fine because the turn ends with error anyway.

  Wait — but there's an ordering concern: it sets `healed = true` then `if (refusal.learnedCap < 1) return false;`. That's intentional.

3. **The latch write happens before the re-send**: the cap latches for the run even if the retry fails. Fine.

4. **Potential issue: `_needsImageCapHeal` vs the message-cap heal ordering.** In `_finishedTurnResult`, the image-cap heal is checked FIRST, before the gh-1680 message-cap heal. If an error message somehow classifies as both... the patterns are distinct; unlikely. Fine.

5. **Key question — does the retry actually go through `_buildRequestContext` with the override?** In `_streamAttempt`, `imageCapOverride: imageCapState.overrideFor(config)`. After `healIfNeeded` sets `learnedCap`, `_AttemptRetry(context)` → the loop presumably retries `_streamAttempt`, which builds with `overrideFor` = learnedCap. Good.

6. **The latch key uses `config.model.provider`**. In the test, provider is 'copilot'. OK.

7. **What about `Agent.copyWith`/`prepareNextTurn` paths** — `imageCapLatches` is included in `copyWith`. Good.

8. **Now a potentially interesting question: `_needsImageCapHeal` checks `imageRegistryConfig.enabled` — the global. But the latch resolution `overrideFor` does NOT check enabled. If registry disabled, heal never fires, and `_buildRequestContext` skips the rewrite entirely under disabled. Fine.

9. **`resolveImageCap` fallback subtlety**: In `_buildRequestContext`, `maxPerRequest: imageCapOverride ?? resolveImageCap(...)`. When there's a learned/latched cap, the perModel config is BYPASED. Wait — `overrideFor` returns `learnedCap ?? latches[key]`. If the latch is 10 (learned from provider), but the user's perModel config says 4, then the override is 10, which is HIGHER than the user config. So the latch (learned) overrides user truth on subsequent requests.

So the latch only exists if the provider refused, meaning provider refused at some cap. Actually wait — the scenario where the latch ends up HIGHER than perModel config: config says 4, request carries ≤4 uniques after rewrite... provider refuses? Only if provider's real cap < 4. Say provider's real cap is 2 → refusal "maximum allowed for model X is 2" → learnedCap=2 → latch=2 → retry at 2. Now subsequent requests use override=2 — that's BELOW the perModel 4, fine and correct.

If user perModel says 4 and provider says the max is 10, then the request would have carried ≤4 (rewritten), so the provider wouldn't have refused... unless the refusal was about something else or the cap text was garbled. Edge case: model id mismatch — the config key is the model id as configured; the provider's refusal names a different id. resolveImageCap uses `config.model.id`. The classifier extracts the provider-named modelId but latches under `config.model.provider|config.model.id`. If they differ (alias), the learned cap could be wrong for the actual model. Hmm, that's an edge case; the latch overrides config silently. Is this worth flaging? Probably a SUGESTION: learned latch could exceed the perModel config cap — the resolution order doc says "latched > perModel config > catalog", so by design latch wins. But "user truth beats built-ins" — the latch isn't built-in, it's provider-measured truth. Actually the provider's measured cap IS more truthful than user config. But wait — there's a subtle bug potential: `imageCapOverride` bypasses the ENTIRE resolution, including `perModel`. If perModel says 2 (user truth, maybe deliberately conservative for cost) and the latch learned 10 for the same pair... can't happen as shown above (config 2 → rewrite to 2 → no refusal if provider cap ≥ 2). If provider cap < 2, learned < 2. So the latch is always ≤ the perModel cap in practice... unless the model-id aliasing issue. OK, negligible; maybe mention as a suggestion.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside

  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no

  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +859
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +859
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T22:35:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

blocks.text:
# pr-1768: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget

## Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

Now I have a good picture of the changes. Let me now do the deep-dive review. Key areas to check:

1. **The image cap resolution in `_buildRequestContext`**: it uses `imageCapOverride ?? resolveImageCap(modelId: config.model.id, catalogMaxImages: config.model.maxImages)`. Note that `resolveImageCap` reads the process-wide `imageRegistryConfig.perModel` — but NOT the `imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest` issue. Wait, actually it does fall back to `imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest`. That's fine.

  BUT: one subtle issue — the doc in agent_loop.dart says "latched > perModel config > catalog maxImages > the global maxPerRequest". The `overrideFor` returns the latch or null; then `resolveImageCap` reads perModel from process-wide `imageRegistryConfig` — this ignores the `ImageRegistryConfig` that was potentially loaded per-host... it IS the process-wide config. OK.

2. **Ordering issue in `healIfNeeded`**: `_needsImageCapHeal` requires `classifyImageCapError(finished.errorMessage) != null`. Then `healIfNeeded` sets `healed = true` BEFORE checking `refusal.learnedCap < 1`. If the cap is degenerate (<1), it returns false — one-shot spent? Actually the docstring says "A degenerate learned cap (< 1, garbage is 0) is refusal-family only: no re-send, the error surfaces as today (E3)." Setting healed=true and returning false means... it's fine because the turn ends with error anyway.

  Wait — but there's an ordering concern: it sets `healed = true` then `if (refusal.learnedCap < 1) return false;`. That's intentional.

3. **The latch write happens before the re-send**: the cap latches for the run even if the retry fails. Fine.

4. **Potential issue: `_needsImageCapHeal` vs the message-cap heal ordering.** In `_finishedTurnResult`, the image-cap heal is checked FIRST, before the gh-1680 message-cap heal. If an error message somehow classifies as both... the patterns are distinct; unlikely. Fine.

5. **Key question — does the retry actually go through `_buildRequestContext` with the override?** In `_streamAttempt`, `imageCapOverride: imageCapState.overrideFor(config)`. After `healIfNeeded` sets `learnedCap`, `_AttemptRetry(context)` → the loop presumably retries `_streamAttempt`, which builds with `overrideFor` = learnedCap. Good.

6. **The latch key uses `config.model.provider`**. In the test, provider is 'copilot'. OK.

7. **What about `Agent.copyWith`/`prepareNextTurn` paths** — `imageCapLatches` is included in `copyWith`. Good.

8. **Now a potentially interesting question: `_needsImageCapHeal` checks `imageRegistryConfig.enabled` — the global. But the latch resolution `overrideFor` does NOT check enabled. If registry disabled, heal never fires, and `_buildRequestContext` skips the rewrite entirely under disabled. Fine.

9. **`resolveImageCap` fallback subtlety**: In `_buildRequestContext`, `maxPerRequest: imageCapOverride ?? resolveImageCap(...)`. When there's a learned/latched cap, the perModel config is BYPASED. Consider: user config sets `perModel.m: 4` (lower). A learned cap of 10 latches for the pair; subsequent turns use the latch (10) — but resolveImageCap would have resolved 4! Wait — `overrideFor` returns `learnedCap ?? latches[key]`. If the latch is 10 (learned from provider), but the user's perModel config says 4, then the override is 10, which is HIGHER than the user config. So the latch (learned) overrides user truth on subsequent requests.

   Hmm, is that a real problem? Scenario: user config `images.perModel.X: 4`. Request with 6 images → the registry caps at 4 → provider never refuses → latch never set. So the latch only exists if the provider refused, meaning provider refused at some cap. Actually wait — the scenario where the latch ends up HIGHER than perModel config: config says 4, request carries ≤4 uniques after rewrite... provider refuses? Only if provider's real cap < 4. Say provider's real cap is 2 → refusal "maximum allowed for model X is 2" → learnedCap=2 → latch=2 → retry at 2. Now subsequent requests use override=2 — that's BELOW the perModel 4, fine and correct.

   But can learnedCap be HIGHER than perModel config? The provider refused with "maximum allowed ... is N". If user perModel says 4 and provider says the max is 10, then the request would have carried ≤4 (rewritten), so the provider wouldn't have refused... unless the refusal was about something else or the cap text was garbled. Edge case: model id mismatch — the config key is the model id as configured; the provider's refusal names a different id. resolveImageCap uses `config.model.id`. The classifier extracts the provider-named modelId but latches under `config.model.provider|config.model.id`. If they differ (alias), the learned cap could be wrong for the actual model. # pr-1768: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget

## Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

Format clean. Now let me do the exhaustive pass — hunt for remaining issues:

1. **`test/model_test.dart` or similar — does `Model.copyWith` have test coverage for maxImages?** Minor.

2. **Check `messageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal` pattern for comparison** — the gh-1680 heal persists learned caps in the policy; the image latch is a plain map. Consistent enough.

3. **Check `_ImageCapHealState.healIfNeeded` — the degenerate-cap ordering bug candidate**: `healed = true` before `if (refusal.learnedCap < 1) return false`. If cap < 1: healed consumed, no re-send — matches E3/IT-6. OK.

4. **Subtle: `overrideFor` returns the latch even when `imageRegistryConfig.enabled == false`?** In `_buildRequestContext` the whole rewrite is inside `if (imageRegistryConfig.enabled)`, so no. And `_needsImageCapHeal` checks enabled. OK.

5. **A REAL correctness question — the interplay between the latch and the per-turn rewriting when the latch is HIGHER than the user's `maxPerRequest` global default.** Scenario: user sets `images.maxPerRequest: 5` globally (their own conservative cap). Provider for model X never refuses (real cap 30). Then `resolveImageCap` returns 5 (no catalog, no perModel) → fine, latch never engaged. Now a refusal happens for another reason? No. So the latch only engages on refusal. When latch = 10 (learned) and the global default is 5: could that happen? First request rewritten to 5 → provider refuses image count only if real cap < 5 → learned ≤ 4 < 5. So no. The learned cap is always ≤ any pre-existing effective cap... except when the effective cap is bypassed: **`imageCapOverride` (the latch) bypasses `perModel` AND the global default on subsequent builds**. As computed, learned ≤ previous effective cap in the scenarios where the previous build rode that cap. But there IS one path where the refused request did NOT ride the cap: when the first request's rewrite happened under a DIFFERENT cap resolution than a later build. E.g., `settings_flow` reload-after-write changes perModel mid-run. Contrived.

  Hmm wait, actually there's one more: **images arriving via `transformContext`** (E5 test) — a host hook can inject MORE images AFTER the rewrite. The rewrite caps the context's images; transformContext runs... let me check the order in `_buildRequestContext`: transformContext is applied FIRST ("pi applies transformContext (then convertToLlm) before each provider call"), then the registry rewrite caps the transformed messages. So injected images ARE capped too. In the E5 test, 'late' rides and total uniques = 10. Confirmed.

6. **Now — check the learned-cap notice + latch when the retry also produces drops**: IT-1 asserts dropNotices has 2 entries on the retry build. Good.

7. **The `imageCapLearnedNotice` fires even when the latch map is null** (config.imageCapLatches == null, runAgentLoop direct callers) — the heal still latches into the local state and notices. Consistent with docs.

8. **Potential double-notice**: `_wireImageCapLearnedNotice` writes dim line + fa.log. Fine.

9. **Security review**: 
  - The regex parses provider error text; extracted `modelId` is interpolated into a CLI dim line via `_style.dim('[images] provider refused: too many images for $modelId — cap learned: $cap; re-sending with fewer images')`. Terminal escape injection? The modelId comes from the provider's error message — a malicious/compromised provider endpoint could embed ANSI escape sequences in the error text, which would be rendered raw into the terminal via `io.writeln`. Is there existing sanitization for provider error text elsewhere? The error message is also surfaced in the transcript as errorMessage normally (pre-existing). The dim-styling wraps the whole line but embedded escapes inside $modelId would pass through. This is a low-severity concern (requires a malicious provider, and provider output is already rendered in transcripts elsewhere — pre-existing pattern). I might raise as a SUGESTION: sanitize/control-chars-strip the interpolated modelId in the notice. Let me check if there's an existing helper for that — e.g., `_logDiagnostic` may sanitize. Let me check how imageDropNotice renders keyPreview and whether anything sanitizes.

5. **A REAL correctness question — the interplay between the latch and the per-turn rewriting when the latch is HIGHER than the user's `maxPerRequest` global default.** Scenario: user sets `images.maxPerRequest: 5` globally (their own conservative cap). Provider for model X never refuses (real cap 30). Then `resolveImageCap` returns 5 (no catalog, no perModel) → fine, latch never engaged. Now a refusal happens for another reason? No. So the latch only engages on refusal. When latch = 10 (learned) and the global default is 5: could that happen? First request rewritten to 5 → provider refuses image count only if real cap < 5 → learned ≤ 4 < 5. So no. The learned cap is always ≤ any pre-existing effective cap... except when the effective cap is bypassed: **`imageCapOverride` (the latch) bypasses `perModel` AND the global default on subsequent builds**. As computed, learned ≤ previous effective cap in the scenarios where the previous build rode that cap. But there IS one path where the refused request did NOT ride the cap: when the first request's rewrite happened under a DIFFERENT cap resolution than a later build. E.g., `settings_flow` reload-after-write changes perModel mid-run. Contrived.

  Hmm wait, actually there's one more: **images arriving via `transformContext`** (E5 test) — a host hook can inject MORE images AFTER the rewrite. The rewrite caps the context's images; transformContext runs... let me check the order in `_buildRequestContext`: transformContext is applied FIRST ("pi applies transformContext (then convertToLlm) before each provider call"), then the registry rewrite caps the transformed messages. So injected images ARE capped too. In the E5 test, 'late' rides and total uniques = 10. Confirmed.

6. **Now — check the learned-cap notice + latch when the retry also produces drops**: IT-1 asserts dropNotices has 2 entries on the retry build. Good.

7. **The `imageCapLearnedNotice` fires even when the latch map is null** (config.imageCapLatches == null, runAgentLoop direct callers) — the heal still latches into the local state and notices. Consistent with docs.

8. **Potential double-notice**: `_wireImageCapLearnedNotice` writes dim line + fa.log. Fine.

9. **Security review**: 
  - The regex parses provider error text; extracted `modelId` is interpolated into a CLI dim line via `_style.dim('[images] provider refused: too many images for $modelId — cap learned: $cap; re-sending with fewer images')`. Provider for model X never refuses (real cap 30). Then `resolveImageCap` returns 5 (no catalog, no perModel) → fine, latch never engaged. Now a refusal happens for another reason? No. So the latch only engages on refusal. When latch = 10 (learned) and the global default is 5: could that happen? First request rewritten to 5 → provider refuses image count only if real cap < 5 → learned ≤ 4 < 5. So no. The learned cap is always ≤ any pre-existing effective cap... except when the effective cap is bypassed: **`imageCapOverride` (the latch) bypasses `perModel` AND the global default on subsequent builds**. As computed, learned ≤ previous effective cap in the scenarios where the previous build rode that cap. But there IS one path where the refused request did NOT ride the cap: when the first request's rewrite happened under a DIFFERENT cap resolution than a later build. Now I understand the heal logic. Important observation: **The pairing heal and message-cap heal run FIRST in the retry loop's one-shot flags — wait no. Actually in `_finishedTurnResult`, the image-cap heal now runs FIRST, before the message-cap heal.** Note ordering: image-cap → message-cap → pairing.

One issue to consider: `healIfNeeded` sets `healed = true` before checking `refusal.learnedCap < 1`. So if the FIRST refusal has a degenerate cap (is 0), `healed = true` and no re-send. If a SECOND refusal (another image-cap error) comes... wait, no — no re-send happens, so the turn ends. But here's a subtle scenario: what if the first refusal is degenerate (`is 0`), no re-send — turn ends with error. Fine.

But what about: first refusal classified with a GOOD cap, re-send happens, retry refusal is an IMAGE-cap refusal again — `healed` already true → falls through to message-cap heal → not classified → pairing heal → not → terminal. Good, matches AC4/IT-2.

Now — a deeper question about `imageCapState.overrideFor(config)` being read at BUILD time in `_streamAttempt`. First attempt: `learnedCap` null, latch map empty → null → `resolveImageCap(modelId, catalogMaxImages)` → say default 20. Request carries 20 uniques... provider refuses at 10 → heal sets learnedCap=10, latch → retry: build with override=10 → rewrite drops to 10 → 200. 

Now — **the second turn of the same run** (same streamed response? no — `_streamAssistantResponse` is per assistant round; `_ImageCapHealState` is created fresh per `_streamAssistantResponse` call, line ~1469). Next round: new state, learnedCap null → `overrideFor` reads the LATCH map → 10. Good — that's the "every later request build for the same pair rides it" behavior. Confirmed working via latch map owned by Agent.

Now the question about **`resolvedCap` interplay with `rewriteHistoryImages`**: when `imageCapOverride` is non-null it bypasses the perModel config. Suppose perModel config = 5 for this model (user truth), and NO catalog entry, and the provider's real cap is 12. Requests are rewritten to ≤5 uniques — never refused. Latch never set. Consistent.

Scenario: perModel config = 5, provider real cap = 3. First request: rewritten to 5 → refused "maximum allowed ... is 3" → learned 3 → latch 3 → retry at 3 → OK. Next rounds: `overrideFor` → latch 3 → correct (3 < 5). Fine.

Can a latch ever be HIGHER than what `resolveImageCap` would return, effectively RAISING a user's cap? Only if the provider's refusal announces a cap HIGHER than the config cap for the same model id — which can't trigger because the request would never carry more than the config cap... UNLESS the rewrite happens only when `imageRegistryConfig.enabled` — fine — or UNLESS the model id in the refusal belongs to a different model. E.g., requests to model A (id "a"), provider's error template names a DIFFERENT model ("maximum allowed for model b is 100") while actually refusing images for a? Contrived. OK — negligible.

Whether a perModel of 50 vs default 20 is allowed — the doc implies ceilings only go DOWN, but the implementation allows going UP. Hmm — is this worth flaging? The old issue #171 `maxPerRequest` is a user-set global cap; perModel overrides can exceed it. Actually wait — re-read the Model.maxImages doc: "A ceiling-seter only — nothing raises a cap above provider reality." That's about the catalog value being measured truth. The implementation just takes the user value verbatim; nothing stops perModel=100 from riding 100 images. But that IS "user truth" — a user explicitly configuring a model cap of 100 gets 100.
